cases.purpose: Truecolor mode: each cell of a 4x2-cell render of a known 4x4 image has the top pixel as foreground and the bottom pixel as background, exactly.
cases.oracle: Unicode terminal model pyte 0.8 (python3-wcwidth) decoding the raw PTY stream; expected cell colours follow the half-block rule documented in the tiv help (top pixel = foreground, bottom pixel = background) and the xterm 256-colour palette (cube index 16+36r+6g+b with levels 0,95,135,175,215,255; greyscale ramp 232..255 = 8+10*(i-232)).
cases.comparison: pyte per-cell fg/bg for all eight cells; rows hold four glyphs each and the next row is blank.

cases.purpose: 256-colour mode: the same image uses palette colours whose RGB values equal the pure red, green, blue, white and black pixels (cube entries 196, 46, 21, 231 and 16).
cases.oracle: Unicode terminal model pyte 0.8 (python3-wcwidth) decoding the raw PTY stream; expected cell colours follow the half-block rule documented in the tiv help (top pixel = foreground, bottom pixel = background) and the xterm 256-colour palette (cube index 16+36r+6g+b with levels 0,95,135,175,215,255; greyscale ramp 232..255 = 8+10*(i-232)). The pixel colours are exactly representable in the xterm cube, so the palette entry colours must equal them.
cases.comparison: pyte per-cell fg/bg (palette resolved to RGB by the decoder) for all eight cells.

cases.purpose: Grey mode: a black-and-white image maps black to the darkest and white to the lightest entry of the xterm greyscale ramp (080808 and eeeeee), top pixel as foreground and bottom pixel as background.
cases.oracle: Unicode terminal model pyte 0.8 (python3-wcwidth) decoding the raw PTY stream; expected cell colours follow the half-block rule documented in the tiv help (top pixel = foreground, bottom pixel = background) and the xterm 256-colour palette (cube index 16+36r+6g+b with levels 0,95,135,175,215,255; greyscale ramp 232..255 = 8+10*(i-232)).
cases.comparison: pyte per-cell fg/bg for all eight cells.

cases.purpose: In the half glyph mode a 16-column render on a terminal exactly 16 cells wide fills each of four rows with 16 single-cell code points: no row wraps into extra lines and the next row stays blank.
cases.oracle: Unicode terminal model pyte 0.8 (python3-wcwidth) decoding the raw PTY stream; expected cell colours follow the half-block rule documented in the tiv help (top pixel = foreground, bottom pixel = background) and the xterm 256-colour palette (cube index 16+36r+6g+b with levels 0,95,135,175,215,255; greyscale ramp 232..255 = 8+10*(i-232)). Block-element, sextant and octant code points are East Asian Width neutral (one cell); a wider glyph would wrap the 16-cell terminal and push content into the blank row.
cases.comparison: Rows 0-3 each hold exactly 16 characters, row 4 is blank (pyte decoded screen).
